rosine-cooks.title: Rosine cooks without recipes.
rosine-cooks.dek: At Dantokpa, one cook turns the morning market into a map of memory, instinct and extraordinary flavor.
body: By six in the morning, Rosine has already tasted the pepper twice. She does not measure it.
Her stall sits where the market begins to fold into the street. Between plantains and charcoal, she makes breakfast for half a neighborhood.

market-names.title: Market names
market-names.dek: Meet the people behind the stalls—the names that make a market more than a place to buy.
body: Every aisle has a voice. Vendors who remember your order, and the season better than any calendar.
This is a short field note on the human infrastructure of Cotonou’s markets.

red-road.title: The red road
red-road.dek: A slower way north—through landscape, food and the people who hold the route together.
body: The road north changes color before it changes speed.
What stays is the invitation to travel with attention, not only arrival.

early-light.title: Early light in Porto-Novo
early-light.dek: Meet the city before breakfast—when Ouando is already in conversation.
body: At first light, baskets change hands and breakfast is ladled from enamel pots.
Porto-Novo rewards the unhurried morning more than the checklist afternoon.

slave-route-note.title: Walking the Slave Route
slave-route-note.dek: A careful account of the path from Place Chacha to the Atlantic.
body: The route is short on the map and long in the body.
What helps is a guide who can name the stations without turning them into a show.

dantokpa-morning.title: Dantokpa before the heat
dantokpa-morning.dek: An early circuit through the great market.
body: Arrive while the air is still almost cool.
Follow someone who works here.

pendjari-dry-season.title: Pendjari in the dry season
pendjari-dry-season.dek: Why the north asks for planning, guides, and respect.
body: The roads lengthen. The air changes.
What you gain is space and real wildlife.

vodun-with-care.title: Vodun, without the caricature
vodun-with-care.dek: How to approach living spiritual practice with respect.
body: Vodun is an official religion here—not the cartoon of dolls and curses.
Visitors who listen more than they film leave with a different country.

possotome-springs.title: The springs at Possotomè
possotome-springs.dek: Thermal water, lake light and a town that refuses to hurry for visitors.
body: Possotomè is introduced first by water: Lake Ahémé, then the springs that have drawn people for reasons older than tourism.
The correct pace is local. Ask before you photograph. Stay long enough to notice who works the shore.

parakou-junction.title: Parakou, where the map turns
parakou-junction.dek: A central-north hub of markets, rail memory and the feeling that the country has changed latitude.
body: Arrive in Parakou and distances rearrange themselves. South feels far; the Sahel edge feels nearer.
Eat where the transport workers eat. The city explains itself better at a shared table than from a moving window.

allada-ordinary.title: Allada under ordinary light
allada-ordinary.dek: Royal memory and market noise share the same streets—history without a velvet rope.
body: Allada is not staged. Lineage and daily traffic occupy the same ground.
Come with a local voice if you can. Silence is part of the visit when the story is heavier than the photo.

ketou-walls.title: Kétou keeps its own time
ketou-walls.dek: A Yoruba town of walls and living culture in the southeast—approach without reducing it to ruins.
body: Kétou’s fortifications and market days still organise a town, not a set.
Walk with someone who can name what you are looking at. Leave room for the present tense.

wagassi-road.title: Following wagassi south
wagassi-road.dek: How a Fulani cheese travels from pastoral north to charcoal grills in the cities.
body: Wagassi begins with milk and knowledge held in families. The calotropis leaf does what recipes only approximate.
By the time it hits a Cotonou grill, it has already crossed regions. Taste is geography made edible.

zem-night.title: The city by zemidjan
zem-night.dek: Motorcycle-taxis as infrastructure, negotiation and a way of reading the night.
body: Zemidjans are not colour. They are how the city breathes after dark—price, trust, shortcut, risk.
Agree the fare before you move. Treat the rider as a professional, not a backdrop.

first-rains.title: When the first rains arrive
first-rains.dek: The shift in markets, roads and mood when the dry season breaks.
body: The first rains change the smell of the ground before they change the calendar.
Travel plans bend. Food shifts. People speak of the season as a character, not a forecast.
